purpose: Work-order task T02: prove the selected solver container runs on this machine before any mesh work.

image.why_pinned: The plan requires an exact digest. The 'latest' tag moves and would break reproducibility.

solver.note: Native ARM64 build, not x86 emulation. Emulated builds would have made the wall-time estimates in the programme proposal meaningless.

tutorial.why_this_case: Steady incompressible RANS with a turbulence model: the same solver class A0.1 and A0.2 will use. A laminar cavity case would not have exercised it.
tutorial.volume_mount_write: confirmed: the container wrote case output to a host-mounted directory

findings: The Docker VM is allocated 7.75 GiB, not the host's 16 GiB. Every mesh-size estimate in the programme proposal was written against 16 GB and is therefore optimistic by roughly a factor of two. Revised working ceiling for a steady incompressible case: order 3-4 million cells, not 6-8 million. The proposal's feasibility table must be corrected or the Docker VM memory raised before A0.2 meshing.

docker manifest inspect returned no manifest for all four candidate images, which initially looked like 'no arm64 build exists'. The Docker Hub registry API showed arm64 manifests for opencfd/openfoam-default tags 2306 and newer. The manifest-inspect failure was a registry/auth artefact, not an absence of arm64. Recorded so the next person does not repeat the false conclusion.
reproduce: docker run --rm --platform linux/arm64 -v "$PWD":/work -w /work opencfd/openfoam-default:2512 bash -lc 'cp -r $FOAM_TUTORIALS/incompressible/simpleFoam/pitzDaily ./case && cd case && blockMesh && checkMesh && simpleFoam'
claim_boundary: A completed tutorial proves the toolchain executes and writes output on this hardware. It proves nothing about mesh adequacy, solution accuracy, or validation for any A0 rung.
